os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session, 37 windows on screen
app: The whole desktop — semantic-compositor router (CGWindowList + per-window channel binding + system-wide hit test). Mirrors windows-desktop-router and linux-desktop-router-merged-view.

stack_detection.method: per-window: process args for a CDP port, then bundle id for AppleScript scriptability, then whether AXUIElementCreateApplication exposes windows
stack_detection.signature: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo returns 37 on-screen windows front-to-back with pid/owner/rect/layer/alpha; each pid then answers (or refuses) its channel probe

channel_setup: campaign/macos/router_mac.py. Accessibility TCC for the AX side; Screen Recording only for verification captures. Privacy rule carried over from the Windows cell: the user's own windows are mapped and channel-classified ONLY — no content walk, nothing of theirs in any artifact. Content extraction is demonstrated exclusively on two windows the agent launched itself (a Chrome with --remote-debugging-port and a throwaway TextEdit document).

t1_read_text.detail: Content pulled live through the bound channel, for owned windows only. Chrome via CDP: 20 tokens, 0.7 ms, vs 720 for a screenshot of the same window. TextEdit via AX: 56 tokens, 6.1–42.3 ms, vs 370–382 in pixels — and the text came back char-exact against the file the harness had just written, including the em-dash. The router never needs the whole screen: it addresses one window through one channel.

t2_enumerate.detail: 37 windows mapped in 31.9 ms into an 838-token merged view, against 1980 tokens for a single full-desktop screenshot (4784 at Retina 2x). Every window was bound to a channel from a signature BEFORE any content was read: 16 accessibility-api, 6 accessibility-api+object-model (TextEdit/Finder/Safari — scriptable bundle ids), 14 pixels-baseline, 1 cdp. The 14 pixel bindings are honest and explicit, not failures: 12 are Control Center menu-bar items that answer AX but expose ZERO windows (frame-only -> 0% structural coverage -> crop, the same shape Windows saw on Unigine Heaven), and 2 are Window Server surfaces where AX refuses outright.

t4_living_screen.detail: Not a living-screen probe; see macos-clock-accessibility-api.

t5_blind_action.detail: No action taken on the user's live desktop — read-only by design. Blind-click mechanics are proven in macos-textedit-accessibility-api and macos-chrome-cdp.

t6_pictorial.detail: Windows with no structural coverage are declared as pixel regions with their rects rather than omitted, so the merged view never reads as an empty desktop.

measurements.notes: THE MEASUREMENT THIS CELL EXISTS FOR — and it is a sharper result than the headline ratio. There are two ways to answer 'which window owns this pixel'. (1) RECONSTRUCT it from the z-order list and the declared rectangles: the first window, front to back, whose rect contains the point. That is the ONLY method available to a Linux or Windows router. (2) ASK THE COMPOSITOR: AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition puts the question to the window server, which answers with the element actually hit. We ran both at 40 overlap points on a real cluttered desktop: global agreement 33/40 = 82.5%, splitting by window LAYER into 33/33 on ordinary windows (kCGWindowLayer == 0) and 0/7 on the overlay layer (1000). AN INDEPENDENT REPLICATION (2026-08-17, same machine, a different 39-window desktop, two identical back-to-back runs) CONFIRMS THE CLASS AND CORRECTS THE RATES: 37/40 global, 32/33 on layer 0, 5/7 on layer 1000 — same overlay window, same mechanism. The per-layer rates are therefore SAMPLE-DEPENDENT, not a law: the overlay declares a 748x264 rect while painting only a small opaque band inside it, so whether an overlay-layer probe point is mis-attributed depends on where that point lands — on the painted band or on the transparent remainder — and the probe points are overlap centres, which move with the desktop. 0/7 and 5/7 are two draws of the same phenomenon; an earlier draft of this cell stated the 0/7 as 'wrong every single time', which generalised one sample and is withdrawn. What IS stable across both desktops: every mis-attribution inside the overlay rect is a FALSE OCCLUSION — fully visible content marked hidden — a silent divergence in the router layer rather than in any app's channel; macOS closes it with one call; and the a-priori signature stays free and exact: kCGWindowLayer > 0 means the declared rect is an UPPER BOUND on what is painted, never a statement of coverage. A Linux/Windows router cannot make that call and must fall back to a per-window pixel spot-check (exactly what src/coverage-guard.mjs does) on every layer>0 surface. The replication also surfaced a SECOND, NARROWER disagreement class that the first sample could not see, on layer 0 itself: at a shared window edge, the window server attributes a ~2-px band (x=756 and 757, for a window whose CGWindowBounds end at x=756) to the window whose AX hittable frame slightly overhangs its declared bounds. Ruled out as causes: map staleness (re-mapped immediately before each hit test, stable across 4 repeats per point) and int() truncation in the router (the raw CGWindowBounds are exact integers). Consequence: layer-0 reconstruction is near-exact but NOT exact — a router should treat any point within ~2 px of a shared window edge as ambiguous and resolve it with the hit test on macOS, or a pixel probe elsewhere.

runtime_verification.method: Screenshot of the disputed region (382,0,748,264) compared against both answers; TextEdit content compared byte-for-byte against the file the harness wrote; Chrome's CDP target list compared against the page the harness opened.
runtime_verification.agreement: The screenshot backs the window server and refutes the z-order reconstruction: the overlay paints a small black band in the menubar area and is transparent elsewhere, with VS Code plainly visible underneath. Owned-window content matched its ground truth exactly on both channels.

permissions_required: Accessibility (TCC) for the AX side and the system-wide hit test
Screen Recording only for the verification screenshot
None for the CDP-bound window (loopback socket)

revisions.what: Occlusion narrative reworded after the independent replication pass: the false-occlusion class and its mechanism replicate (same overlay window), but the 100%/0% per-layer dichotomy does not — replication measured 32/33 on layer 0 and 5/7 on layer 1000, so the rates are now stated as sample-dependent, and a second, narrower ~2-px shared-edge disagreement class on layer 0 is recorded. The headline cost figures and the a-priori layer signature are unchanged. See campaign/results/verification/macos-replication.md.
